docs.title: recast
docs.text:
recast corrects a crystal structure relaxed with density-functional theory (DFT) or with a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) towards the experimental structure: the cell and every atomic position. It is the code of RECAST (refinement of calculated structures).

From the atom descriptors of the pretrained MLIP MACE-OMAT-0, the correction predicts how the length of every atom pair within 5 angstrom should change, and least-squares fits turn these changes into a Green-Lagrange strain of the cell and displacements of the atoms. In the main fit the predicted changes act as a missing energy, balanced against the Hessian of MACE-OMAT-0, so that the structure yields along its soft deformations. The fits are equivariant, and the corrected structure keeps the space group of the calculated one. On Materials Project crystals held out of training the mean errors fall from 4.12 to 0.85 % in volume, from 0.93 to 0.64 % in cell shape and from 1.65 to 0.86 % in bond lengths, against experimental structures of the Crystallography Open Database (Validation).

  • Get started: install recast and correct a first structure.
  • Web page: the correction in the browser.
  • How-to: correct a structure, use another MLIP, retrain.
  • Theory: the equations of the paper's Methods and Supplementary Information and the functions that implement them.
  • Reference: command line, Python API.
  • Citing.

docs.title: Citing
docs.text:
If you use recast, cite the paper:

U. Singh, P. Costa Carvalho, E. K. Delczeg-Czirjak, O. Eriksson and S. I. Simak, Correcting calculated crystal structures towards experiment, in preparation (2026).

@unpublished{singh2026recast,
  author = {Singh, Utkarsh and Costa Carvalho, Pamela and Delczeg-Czirjak, Erna K. and Eriksson, Olle and
            Simak, Sergei I.},
  title  = {Correcting calculated crystal structures towards experiment},
  note   = {In preparation},
  year   = {2026}
}

A correction also uses MACE-OMAT-0 and the D3(BJ) dispersion correction; cite them as well:

  • I. Batatia et al., MACE: higher order equivariant message passing neural networks for fast and accurate force fields, NeurIPS (2022); the MACE-OMAT-0 model of the ACEsuit/mace-foundations release.
  • L. Barroso-Luque et al., Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) inorganic materials dataset and models (2024), the training data of MACE-OMAT-0.
  • S. Grimme, J. Antony, S. Ehrlich and H. Krieg, J. Chem. Phys. 132, 154104 (2010); S. Grimme, S. Ehrlich and L. Goerigk, J. Comput. Chem. 32, 1456 (2011).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install "recast[features] @ git+https://github.com/utksi/recast"

recast needs Python 3.9 or newer. The features extra installs PyTorch, ASE, spglib, h5py, mace-torch 0.3.16 and torch-dftd 0.5.3, the versions of the paper's runs.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
A correction uses two sets of weights. Neither is part of the package.

Model Source Option MACE-OMAT-0 (medium) downloaded from the ACEsuit/mace-foundations release on first use, sha256 checked --mace FILE RECAST networks the Hugging Face repository utksi/recast-models --release DIR

Downloads are cached in ~/.cache/recast (set RECAST_CACHE to change it) and in the Hugging Face cache.

docs.title: Correct a structure
docs.text:
recast correct POSCAR -o corrected

The input is any file that ASE reads: a VASP POSCAR, a CIF, an extended XYZ file. The command prints the lattice parameters before and after, the strain, and the five strain estimates with their spread, and writes corrected.vasp, corrected.cif, summary.txt and summary.json into the output folder.

The same in Python:

import recast

res = recast.correct("POSCAR", out="corrected")
print(res["vol_change"], res["spread_shape"])

On one CPU core a correction of a cell with a few atoms takes 15 to 30 s once the models are cached (the first run downloads them), most of it in the two relaxations with MACE-OMAT-0 and in the Hessian.

docs.title: Theory
docs.text: The equations of the Methods of the paper and those of its Supplementary Information that the code implements (numbers S1, S2, ...), with their numbers there, in the notation of the code. The strain of the cell is the Green-Lagrange strain E. Each equation links to the function that implements it; the comment directly above that function states the same equation, and tools/check_equations.py checks that it does.

docs.title: (1) Deformation of the calculated structure
docs.text:
L_hat = L U, f_hat = f + u L^-1, U = (I + 2E)^(1/2), so that r_hat_k = (r_k + u_k) U

Implemented by recast.predict.corrected.

L cell rows (angstrom), f fractional coordinates, r_k = f_k L, E a symmetric Green-Lagrange strain, u_k displacements (angstrom). U is the symmetric stretch, defined when lambda_min(I + 2E) > 0.

docs.title: (2) Strain target
docs.text:
E = 1/2 (L_ref^-1 G_tgt L_ref^-T - I), G_tgt = L_tgt L_tgt^T

Implemented by recast.geometry.green.

With L_ref the calculated cell and L_tgt the experimental one this is E, so that L_tgt = L_ref (I + 2E)^(1/2) R_0 with R_0 orthogonal and det(I + 2E)^(1/2) = V/V.

docs.title: (3) Displacement target
docs.text:
u*_k = (f_e,k - f_c,k) L_c - (1/n) sum_l (f_e,l - f_c,l) L_c

Implemented by recast.targets.displacement_target.

f_c are the calculated fractional coordinates unwrapped to the image nearest the experimental ones f_e.

docs.title: (4) Error measures
docs.text:
e_V = |J_hat / J* - 1|, e_S = |S(E_hat) - S(E*)|_F,
e_L = (1/3) sum_i |(G_hat_ii / G*_ii)^(1/2) - 1|, e_A = (1/3) sum_{j<k} |phi_jk(G_hat) - phi_jk(G*)|,
e_B = (1/|B|) sum_b |ln(d_hat_b / d*_b)|, e_D = ((1/n') sum_{k not H} |u_hat_k - u*_k - t|^2)^(1/2)

Implemented by recast.errors.structure_errors.

J = det(I + 2E)^(1/2), S(E) = 1/2 ln(J^(-2/3) (I + 2E)) the shape, G = L (I + 2E) L^T, phi_jk the cell angles, B the first-shell bonds of the experimental structure between atoms other than hydrogen, t the mean of u_hat_k - u*_k over the n' atoms other than hydrogen.

docs.title: (5) eSEN-30M-OMat descriptors averaged with the inversion image
docs.text:
x_k = [s_k(S) + s_k(I S)] / 2

Implemented by recast.esen.descriptors.

For the variant of the cell estimators. s_k the l = 0 rows of the node embedding of atom k after each of the ten blocks (1,280 values), I S the inversion image of the structure S (fractional coordinates -f mod 1, same cell).

docs.title: (6) Hessian on the retained modes
docs.text:
S H S = U diag(w) U^T, S = diag(g_K / V^(1/3), I); H_ret = S^-1 U_k diag(w_k) U_k^T S^-1 over w_k > TOL

Implemented by recast.features.retained.

g_K = (1, 1, 1, sqrt 2, sqrt 2, sqrt 2); (w_k, U_k) the eigenpairs of S H S; TOL = 1e-3 eV/angstrom^2. H is the exact Green-Lagrange Hessian of MACE-OMAT-0 (equation S2); H_ret has zero stiffness along the removed modes.

docs.title: (7) Pair targets and weights
docs.text:
s_p = 1e-2 o_0, w_p = f_c(d_p) exp(clip(o_1, -3, 3)), (o_0, o_1) = MLP_p(z_p)

Implemented by recast.networks.DLSNet.forward.

s_p is a target Green strain of pair p, (d'^2 / d^2 - 1) / 2; z_p the invariant pair features (equation S5).

docs.title: (8) Direct strain head (estimator 1)
docs.text:
E_d = 1e-2 [t I / 3 + (1/n) sum_i (a_i T_i + c_i dev(T_i T_i))] + sum_k m_k [c_k dev T_k + d_k tr(T_k) I / 3],
T_i = sum over the pairs p containing i of w_p dev(r_hat_p r_hat_p^T)

Implemented by recast.networks.StrainNet.forward.

(a_i, c_i), t and (c_k, d_k) are outputs of networks on invariants; w_p the bond weights of the head; T_k the Green-Lagrange relaxation strains (equation S3) and m_k their masks.

docs.title: (9) Linearized Green strain of a pair
docs.text:
a_p . q = r_hat_p^T E r_hat_p + r_hat_p . (u_j - u_i) / d_p

Implemented by recast.fits.pair_rows.

q = (gamma, u), gamma the engineering Voigt vector of E; a_p is the row of pair p; exact at u = 0.

docs.title: (10) Distance-least-squares fit (estimators 2 and 3)
docs.text:
(A + Lam) q = r, Lam = diag(lam_g RG, lam_u I)

Implemented by recast.fits.solve_free.

A = sum_p w_p a_p a_p^T and r = sum_p w_p s_p a_p (recast.fits.normal_eq), RG = diag(1, 1, 1, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2); estimator 2 solves for the strain alone (u = 0).

docs.title: (11) Missing energy of the pair restraints
docs.text:
Delta E(q) = kappa0 / 2 sum_p w_p (a_p . q - s_p)^2 = q^T A q / 2 - r . q + const

Implemented by recast.fits.normal_eq.

A and r computed with the spring constants kappa0 w_p.

docs.title: (12) Hessian-regularized distance-least-squares fit (estimator 4)
docs.text:
M q = kappa_0 b, M = P H P + kappa_0 (A + Lam_0)

Implemented by recast.estimators.Member.solve.

P removes the three rigid translations from the Hessian H (equation 6, float64); Lam_0 the ridge term of equation 10.

docs.title: (13) Hessian-regularized fit with a strain prior (estimator 5)
docs.text:
(P H P + K A + Lam_d + Lam) q = K r + Lam_d q_d

Implemented by recast.networks.UnifiedNet.forward.

K = kappa exp(z_K), Lam_d = diag(lam_V P_V + lam_S P_S, 0) with lam_V, lam_S = K (sum_p w_p) exp(z_V, z_S), q_d = (gamma(E_d), 0), (z_V, z_S, z_K) = 4 tanh(o / 4).

docs.title: (14) Mean strain
docs.text:
E_hat = (1 / M) sum_m E_m

Implemented by recast.estimators.mean_strain.

The arithmetic mean over all cell members, equal to the mean over the five estimators of their means over the initializations; a mean with lambda_min(I + 2E_hat) <= 1e-6 has no cell and returns the calculated structure.

docs.title: (15) Atoms at a given cell
docs.text:
u = (A_uu + lam_u I)^-1 (r_u - A_ug gamma_c)

Implemented by recast.fits.solve_clamped.

A and r of the Hessian-regularized fit (equation 12), so that A_uu + lam_u I = M_uu and r_u = kappa_0 b_u.

docs.title: (S2) Green-Lagrange Hessian
docs.text:
H = d2W/dq2 at q = 0 = [[K, Lam^T], [Lam, Phi]],
W(q) the energy of the cell L U and positions (r + u) U, U = (I + 2E(gamma))^(1/2), by automatic differentiation

Implemented by recast.features.mace_hessian.

K = V C0 (eV) the strain block, Lam (eV/angstrom) the internal-strain coupling, Phi (eV/angstrom^2) the force constants, all in float64; recast.features.hessian_fd gives the same matrix by central differences for any ASE calculator.

docs.title: (S3) Relaxation strains
docs.text:
T1 = E(L, L_1), T0 = E(L, L_0), D = T1 - T0

Implemented by recast.features.relaxation_tensors.

E(L, L') = 1/2 (L^-1 L' L'^T L^-T - I); L_0 and L_1 the cells relaxed with MACE-OMAT-0 without and with D3; the networks read T1 and D, each with a mask that is 1 when its relaxations converged.

docs.title: (S4) Channel quadrupoles of the atoms
docs.text:
Q_i^k = sum over the pairs p containing i of f_k(p) dev(r_hat_p r_hat_p^T),
f_k(p) = MLP_q(h_i + h_j, h_i * h_j, rbf(d_p)) f_c(d_p)

Implemented by recast.networks.DLSNet.quadrupoles.

h_i the embedded descriptors, rbf 16 Gaussians, f_c the cosine cutoff at 5 angstrom, k = 1..8.

docs.title: (S5) Invariant features of a pair
docs.text:
z_p = (h_i + h_j, h_i * h_j, rbf(d_p), {o_i^k + o_j^k, o_i^k o_j^k, tr(Q_i^k Q_j^k),
r_hat_p^T (Q_i^k Q_j^k + Q_j^k Q_i^k) r_hat_p / 2}_k, chi_U, g, {100 m_k r_hat_p^T T_k r_hat_p, 100 m_k tr T_k,
m_k}_k), o_i^k = r_hat_p^T Q_i^k r_hat_p

Implemented by recast.networks.DLSNet.pair_features.

chi_U the Hubbard-U flag, g the structure mean of h_i, T_k and m_k the relaxation strains and their masks.

docs.title: (S6) Cell loss
docs.text:
joint rho(s2 + t2) or decoupled rho(s2) + rho(t2), mean over the batch, with s2 = |S(E_hat) - S(E*)|_F^2,
t2 = w0 (ln J(E_hat) - ln J(E*))^2 / 3, rho(x) = delta^2 (sqrt(1 + x / delta^2) - 1)

Implemented by recast.losses.cell_loss.

The loss of the error measures themselves (S the shape, ln J the log volume ratio), evaluated in float64 by a Cayley transform and the atanh series (recast.losses); a prediction outside the domain gets the quadratic form of the same loss at its target.

docs.title: (S7) Atom loss
docs.text:
rho(L_g + wb L_b + wu sum um (q - q*)^2)

Implemented by recast.losses.atom_loss.

L_b the weighted mean squared linearized bond-length error over the first-shell bonds without hydrogen, um = 1 / (n' dbar^2) on the atoms other than hydrogen; at the experimental cell L_g = 0.

docs.title: (S8) Corrected resampled t-test
docs.text:
t = dbar / sqrt((1/J + n2/n1) s_d^2)

Implemented by recast.score.corrected_t.

d_j the paired fold differences, J folds, n2 and n1 the test and training sizes; J - 1 degrees of freedom.

docs.title: Errors on held-out structures
docs.text:
The released DFT networks, scored on the test sets of ten random splits of 18,056 structure pairs, each a current PBE or PBE+U structure of the Materials Project matched with an experimental structure of the Crystallography Open Database (17,937 test predictions; pairs whose experimental structure appears in OMat24 are left out). Mean over the ten test-set means, with the standard deviation over the splits in parentheses.

Error DFT structure corrected volume e_V (%) 4.122 (0.040) 0.849 (0.030) cell shape e_S (%) 0.933 (0.020) 0.643 (0.011) lattice-vector lengths e_L (%) 1.427 (0.015) 0.424 (0.010) cell angles e_A (degrees) 0.110 (0.003) 0.077 (0.003) bond lengths e_B (%) 1.645 (0.027) 0.856 (0.022) bond angles e_theta (degrees) 0.906 (0.029) 0.779 (0.024) atomic positions e_D (angstrom) 0.043 (0.001) 0.035 (0.001)

No test prediction had a mean strain outside the domain (lambda_min(I + 2E) > 0 for all 18,060 predictions).

For structures relaxed with the two MLIPs (--source), the corrections retrained on their relaxations lower the mean errors on the same 17,937 test predictions from 4.72 to 0.89 % in volume, from 1.20 to 0.73 % in cell shape and from 1.68 to 0.85 % in bond lengths (TECE-OAM-RRA-1.0), and from 4.77 to 0.98 %, from 1.22 to 0.75 % and from 1.68 to 0.88 % (EquFlashV2-45M-OAM).

The error measures are those of equation 4 (Theory). The paper gives the errors of grouped folds without shared structure prototypes or chemical systems, and of the ablations.

docs.title: Use another MLIP
docs.text: The released networks expect their inputs from MACE-OMAT-0 and from no other potential. Features of another potential give them inputs they were not trained on. To use another potential, write a featurizer for it, check it, and retrain the networks with the pipeline (Retrain).

docs.title: The four inputs
docs.text:
A featurizer (recast.featurizers.Featurizer) computes any of the four inputs of the networks from a calculated structure, and each input may come from its own featurizer:

Input Shipped networks What it is cell none (the atoms descriptors) per-atom descriptors of the cell networks, when they differ from atoms atoms MACE-OMAT-0 per-atom descriptors of the networks hessian MACE-OMAT-0 the Green-Lagrange Hessian H (blocks K, Lam, Phi), stored on its retained modes in float64 relax MACE-OMAT-0 + D3(BJ) the Green-Lagrange relaxation strains T1 (with dispersion), D = T1 - T0, and their masks

recast.featurizers.Inputs names the featurizer of each input. write_features computes them for a list of structures and records the name of each featurizer in features.json. A release records the names it was trained with, and recast correct refuses features from other models.

docs.title: A featurizer from any ASE calculator
docs.text:
ASEFeaturizer needs only an ASE calculator and a descriptor function. The Hessian follows by central differences of the calculator's gradient in the coordinates q = (gamma(E), u) (recast.features.hessian_fd: the stress and the forces of the deformed structure, steps 1e-3 in strain and 1e-3 angstrom), and the relaxations by ASE (FixSymmetry, FrechetCellFilter, FIRE, fmax 0.01 eV/angstrom), the second one with D3(BJ) added. A potential written in PyTorch can give the exact Hessian by automatic differentiation instead, as MACEFeaturizer.hessian does.

from recast.featurizers import ASEFeaturizer, Inputs


def my_calculator(precision):
    """The potential as an ASE calculator; precision is 'float32' (first relaxation stage) or 'float64'."""
    from my_mlip import MyCalculator

    return MyCalculator(dtype=precision)


def my_descriptors(Z, f, L):
    """Per-atom invariant descriptors (n x D) of the structure with atomic numbers Z, fractional coordinates f and
    cell rows L (angstrom), for example the scalar channels of every layer of the network."""
    ...


feat = ASEFeaturizer(my_calculator, my_descriptors, name="my-mlip")
inputs = Inputs(cell=None, atoms=feat, hessian=feat, relax=feat)

Save a function that returns inputs in an importable module, and give it to the commands as --inputs my_module:my_inputs. A subclass of Featurizer can instead override descriptors, calculator, hessian or relaxations; MACEFeaturizer and ESENFeaturizer are two examples.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
recast.contract measures what the networks rely on: descriptors invariant under rotations, reflections and translations, a Hessian that transforms with the structure, relaxation strains that rotate with it, and the blocks K, Lam and Phi of the Hessian against second differences of the energy.

from recast import contract as C
import numpy as np

v = C.hessian_violation(feat, Z, f, L, Q=np.diag([-1.0, 1, 1]))  # a mirror
u = C.units_check(feat, Z, f, L)

tests/test_featurizer_contract.py runs these checks in double precision. MACE-OMAT-0 passes them to rounding. eSEN-30M-OMat passes them under rotations and translations but not under reflections: its energy is not invariant under improper operations, and its Hessian changes by 0.6 % (median) and up to 4.6 % under them. Its descriptors can be averaged with the inversion image, which makes them invariant (recast.esen, used by the paper's variant of the cell estimators); its Hessian cannot be repaired that way. A new potential whose Hessian fails the reflection check will break the space group of corrected structures.

docs.title: Correct a structure
docs.text:
recast correct STRUCTURE [--source dft|tece_oam_rra|equflashv2_oam] [--functional PBE|PBE+U] [--given FILE]
                         [--symmetrize TOL] -o OUT

docs.title: What the structure must be
docs.text: A periodic, ordered crystal: three lattice vectors and no two atoms closer than 0.5 angstrom (a partially occupied site read as several atoms is refused). The networks were trained on PBE and PBE+U structures of the Materials Project matched with experimental structures of the Crystallography Open Database, and on relaxations of those experimental structures with two MLIPs. They correct structures of that kind.

docs.title: Source and functional
docs.text: --source dft (the default) is for PBE and PBE+U relaxations. Give --functional PBE+U for a DFT+U calculation: the networks read a flag for it. --source tece_oam_rra and --source equflashv2_oam select the networks retrained for structures relaxed with TECE-OAM-RRA-1.0 and EquFlashV2-45M-OAM; these take no functional flag.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
File Content corrected.vasp, corrected.cif the corrected structure, atoms in the input order summary.txt lattice parameters before and after, the Green-Lagrange strain, the five estimates and their spread summary.json the same numbers and the arrays (E, u, E_r, Lh, fh), lam_min and invalid given_cell.vasp, given_cell.cif with --given: the atoms placed at the given cell

The corrected cell is L (I + 2E)^(1/2) and the atoms (r_k + u_k) (I + 2E)^(1/2), with E the mean of five Green-Lagrange strain estimates (Theory). A mean with no cell, lambda_min(I + 2E) <= 1e-6, returns the calculated structure and sets invalid; no test prediction of the paper was such a case. The spread of the five estimates is larger for less reliable corrections: on the test sets, the tenth of the structures with the largest shape spread had 2.6 times the mean shape error.

docs.title: Atoms at a cell of your choice
docs.text: --given FILE places the atoms at another cell: a structure file whose cell is used, or a JSON file with {"cell": [[...], [...], [...]]} (rows, angstrom, in the lattice basis of the input) or a Green-Lagrange strain {"strain": [E11, E22, E33, 2E23, 2E13, 2E12]}. A cell whose log stretch 1/2 ln(I + 2E) has a principal value beyond 0.2 is refused, as it means another lattice basis.

docs.title: Exact symmetry
docs.text: The prediction keeps the space group of the input in exact arithmetic. --symmetrize TOL projects the strain and the displacements onto the space group that spglib finds at TOL angstrom, which removes the asymmetry left by float32 networks and by inputs that are symmetric only to about TOL.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
import recast

res = recast.correct("POSCAR", source="dft", functional="PBE+U", symmetrize=1e-3, out="corrected")

recast.correct also takes an ase.Atoms object and returns the dictionary of summary.json. Without out it writes no file.

docs.title: Retrain
docs.text: The pipeline takes structure pairs (a calculated structure and the experimental structure it corresponds to, with the same atoms in the same order) to a release folder that recast correct uses. The commands below run it on a synthetic set built from ASE prototypes, so that every step can be tried without data; tests/test_pipeline.py runs the same commands with four epochs per member in about one minute on one core.

docs.title: 1. Pairs
docs.text:
recast toy -o work/pairs.json

writes 39 pairs: fcc, bcc and hcp cells of seven metals and B2, L1_2 and L1_0 alloys as calculated structures, each deformed by a known strain and known displacements as its experimental structure (recast.toy). Your own pairs file has the same layout, a JSON list of

{"key": "...", "functional": "PBE", "Z": [...],
 "calculated": {"L": [[...], [...], [...]], "f": [[...], ...]},
 "experimental": {"L": [[...], [...], [...]], "f": [[...], ...]}}

with cell rows L in angstrom and fractional coordinates f.

docs.title: 2. Targets
docs.text:
recast targets work/pairs.json -o work/targets.h5

computes the strain and displacement targets of every pair (recast.targets): the Green-Lagrange strain from the calculated to the experimental cell, in the lattice basis that fits the atoms best, and the displacements where the atoms of the two structures correspond.

docs.title: 3. Features
docs.text:
recast features work/targets.h5 -o work/data --inputs toy

computes the inputs of the calculated structures and stores them with the targets. --inputs toy uses ASE's EMT potential and radial descriptors; --inputs shipped uses MACE-OMAT-0 (descriptors, the exact Green-Lagrange Hessian and the D3 relaxations), and --inputs MODULE:FUNCTION your own featurizers (Use another MLIP).

For many structures, split the work into shards (on a GPU with --device cuda) and merge them:

recast features work/targets.h5 -o work/shards/0 --inputs shipped --device cuda --shard 0/8
...                                                                              # shards 1 to 7, e.g. as array tasks
recast features work/targets.h5 -o work/data --merge work/shards/*

Each structure is stored as soon as it is done; --resume continues an interrupted shard in its folder. The merged folder is the same as the folder of one run over all structures.

docs.title: 4. Partitions
docs.text:
recast split work/data -o work/parts.json --keys 42,43 --test 0.15 --val 0.15

draws one random partition into training, validation and test structures per key: a permutation by the key, the test set first, then the validation set from the rest (--val is the share of the rest). The paper used ten keys (42 to 51), 1,806 test pairs per key (10 %) and 10 % of the rest for validation; data/structure_pairs.csv lists its assignment of the pairs. When one material has several pairs (for example several experimental reports), give a CSV key,unit with --units, so that all pairs of a material fall on one side.

Every choice of settings is made on the development pool, the pairs in no test set, so that each test set is scored once by the final networks. The development folds and the grouped evaluation folds of the paper:

recast groups work/data -o work/groups.csv                       # reduced formula, prototype, chemical system
recast folds --partitions work/parts.json --groups work/groups.csv -o work/folds.json \
    --random 3000,3010 --formula 3100 --prototype 3200 --seed 20261022
recast folds --partitions work/parts.json -o work/folds_more.json --add-to work/folds.json --random 3040 --seed 7
recast grouped work/data --groups work/groups.csv -o work/grouped.json --prototype 4200 --chemsys 4300
recast fraction work/parts.json -o work/parts_f25.json --fraction 0.25            # learning curves
recast table --splits work/parts.json --folds work/folds.json work/grouped.json -o work/pairs.csv

recast table --columns ids.csv adds further identifier columns after the first (a CSV keyed by the pair), as the COD ids and the functional of data/structure_pairs.csv.

Five folds per family; the random families are drawn with one generator, the formula and prototype families keep each group on one side; a later round of choices gets a fresh random family (--add-to) that no earlier choice was scored on. The grouped evaluation folds hold out every prototype (4200 to 4204) or every chemical system (4300 to 4304) once. These commands rebuild the paper's development folds, grouped folds and training fractions exactly from its pairs and splits, and data/structure_pairs.csv byte for byte (tests/test_partitions.py).

docs.title: 5. Members
docs.text:
recast members --data work/data --partitions work/parts.json --keys 42,43 --runs work/runs -- --epochs 20

trains the 18 members of every key: the five strain estimators (presets A0, aff, full, spr30, uni) and the atom fit (sat), three initializations each, with the hyperparameters of the paper's DFT correction (recast.train.PRESETS); --presets restricts the member types. On a cluster, write one line per member type, seed and key and run them as a job array:

recast jobs --data work/data --partitions work/parts.json --keys 42,43 --runs work/runs -o work/lines.txt \
    --device cuda --sbatch work/train.sbatch --account ACCOUNT --partition gpu --time 02:30:00 --gpus 1 -- --epochs 300
mkdir -p logs && sbatch work/train.sbatch

The lines give the same members as recast members (each key is seeded at its start). Every member minimizes the volume and shape errors of its strain (the cell loss of the Theory page). Options after -- go to recast train, which trains one member type and accepts every hyperparameter on the command line. The MLIP corrections of the paper used their own settings; their values are in the args_<key>.json files of the released networks.

docs.title: 6. Selection and scores
docs.text:
recast select --data work/data --keys 42,43 --metric cell:shape work/runs/A0_s0 work/runs/A0_s1

compares candidate runs by the mean over the keys of a test-set error (cell:shape for a cell member, the bond-length error at the experimental cell cellO+final:bond for the atom fit) and marks the lowest. In the paper, candidates were compared on the development folds only; the reported test sets were scored once.

docs.title: 7. Release and test errors
docs.text:
recast export --runs work/runs --keys 42,43 --data work/data -o work/release
recast evaluate --release work/release --data work/data --partitions work/parts.json --keys 42,43 -o work/scores.json
recast correct new.vasp --release work/release --inputs toy -o work/out

export writes the release folder (manifest.json with the sha256 of every file and the names of the featurizers, members/<tag>/). evaluate scores each key's own test structures with that key's members: the mean of the 15 cell members' strains and the atoms of the three atom-fit members. correct then uses the release like the published one.

docs.title: recast.featurizers
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Featurizers: the pretrained models that compute the inputs of the networks from a calculated structure, pluggable in the way ASE calculators are. A featurizer gives any of four inputs, and each input of a features folder may come from its own featurizer (Inputs): cell per-atom descriptors of the cell networks (estimators 1 to 5), when they differ from the atom ones atoms per-atom descriptors of the atom-fit networks (and of the cell networks when cell is None) hessian the Hessian H of the energy in Green-Lagrange (G-L) coordinates, stored as its retained modes H_ret relax the relaxation strains T1, T0, D = T1 - T0 (G-L) and their masks The networks of the paper read MACE-OMAT-0 for every input (SHIPPED: descriptors of every layer, the exact Hessian by automatic differentiation, the D3 relaxations); they expect exactly these. Another potential means retraining with the pipeline (recast.train).

Conventions: Z atomic numbers, f fractional coordinates (n x 3), L cell rows (angstrom); coordinates q = (gamma, u), gamma = (E_11, E_22, E_33, 2 E_23, 2 E_13, 2 E_12) the engineering Voigt vector of the G-L strain E of the cell and u (n x 3) Cartesian displacements; the deformed structure has the cell L U and positions (r + u) U, U = (I + 2E)^(1/2).

Mathematics (recast.features gives the details): H = d2W/dq2 at q = 0 = [[K, Lam^T], [Lam, Phi]] (eV, eV/angstrom, eV/angstrom^2), W the potential's energy: by automatic differentiation for MACE (recast.features.mace_hessian), else by central differences of the gradient g(q) of any ASE calculator (recast.features.hessian_fd: h = 1e-3 in gamma and 1e-3 angstrom in u) H_ret: the modes of the Kelvin-scaled S H S above 1e-3 eV/angstrom^2 (recast.features.retained) T1 = E(L, L_1), T0 = E(L, L_0), D = T1 - T0: G-L strains to the minima of the potential with (1) and without (0) the dispersion term (D3(BJ) by default), masks (c_1, c_0, c_1 c_0) (recast.features.relaxation_tensors) Contract of a featurizer (tests/test_featurizer_contract.py, recast.contract): under r -> r Q^T + t for any orthogonal Q (rotations and reflections) and translation t, the descriptors are unchanged and, in Kelvin-scaled strain coordinates, H -> R H R^T with R = diag(K, I_n kron Q), K the Kelvin representation of Q on symmetric strains.

docs.title: recast.esen
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

eSEN-30M-OMat (fairchem-core 1.10.0: esen_backbone with the esen_mlp_efs_head_dens energy head) in plain PyTorch, read from the official checkpoint file esen_30m_omat.pt (gated repository facebook/OMAT24; its licence applies, and no weight is copied into this package). It gives the descriptors of the eSEN variant of the cell networks (the released networks do not use them), and energies, forces, stresses and the Hessian, without fairchem.

Conventions: positions r_k (n x 3, angstrom), cell rows L (3 x 3, angstrom), Z atomic numbers; edge e = (s_e -> t_e) with integer image shift m_e, s the neighbour and t the centre (fairchem's radius_graph_pbc order). Constants of the checkpoint: C = 128 channels, lmax = 3, mmax = 2, 10 blocks, cutoff r_c = 6 angstrom, 64 Gaussians, at most 300 neighbours per atom.

Mathematics

strain D (3 x 3) = 0 with gradient, E = (D + D^T)/2, r' = r + r E, L' = L + L E edges v_e = r's - r'_t + m_e L', d_e = |v_e|, every pair with 1e-2 angstrom < d_e <= r_c edge frame u = v/d, set to (0, +-1, 0) when |u_y| > 0.999999 (fairchem's rot_clip); a vector w drawn uniformly in [-0.5, 0.5)^3, normalized, replaced by (-w_y, w_x, w_z) or (w_x, -w_z, w_y) when better conditioned; z = u x w / |.|, y = u x z / |.|; rotation M with rows (z, u, -y) Wigner D D^l = Z_l(alpha) J_l Z_l(beta) J_l Z_l(gamma), with the angles of M (e3nn's xyz_to_angles written without angles); Z_l(t) has cos(k t) on the diagonal and sin(k t) on the antidiagonal (k = l - i) embeddings h_t (16 x C) in l-major (l, m) order, h_t[0] = emb(Z_t); edge features f_e = [exp(c (d_e - mu_k)^2) (64), src_emb(Z_s), tgt_emb(Z_t)]; degree embedding h_t += sum_e D^T rad(f_e)(m = 0) env(d_e / r_c) / 5, env(x) = (1 - x)^3 (1 + 3x + 6x^2 + 10x^3 + 15x^4) for x < 1, else 0 block k h += sum_{e -> t} D^T SO2_2(gate(SO2_1([h_s, h_t] rotated by D, rad_k(f_e)))) env(d_e / r_c); h += SpectralAtomwise(RMSNorm(h)) energy U = sum_k MLP(RMSNorm(h)_k[0]) + sum_k ref(Z_k) (eV) forces F = -dU/dr (eV/angstrom); stress sigma = (1/V) dU/dD (eV/angstrom^3, ASE sign), V = |det L| Hessian Phi = d^2 U / dr dr (eV/angstrom^2), rows by a second backward pass descriptors s_k(S) = [h_k^(1)[0], ..., h_k^(10)[0]] (n x 1280): the l = 0 row of the node embedding after each block; x_k = [s_k(S) + s_k(I S)] / 2, I S the inversion image (f -> -f mod 1, same cell)

Every per-edge quantity is invariant under the draw of w up to rounding (the network is equivariant under rotations), so any draw gives the same outputs to rounding; the draws here are fixed (seeded) per edge. The network is not equivariant under reflections, which is why the descriptors are averaged with the inversion image.

docs.title: recast.features
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Input features of the correction, every one computed from the calculated structure alone (no experimental quantity): the MACE-OMAT-0 Hessian in Green-Lagrange (G-L) coordinates, the pairs within the cutoff and the structure's own first-shell bonds, the two D3 relaxation strains, and the per-atom descriptors of MACE-OMAT-0 (and, for training other variants, of eSEN-30M-OMat). write_features() (and recast.featurizers.write_features for any choice of models) stores them in a folder; load_new() reads the folder into the inputs of the predictors. esen_calculator(), esen_descriptors() and write_esen_descriptors() are the fairchem path, kept as the reference of recast.esen (they need fairchem-core 1.10).

Conventions: L cell rows (angstrom), f fractional coordinates (n x 3), r_k = f_k L, Z atomic numbers, V = |det L|, energies in eV. Strains are engineering Voigt vectors gamma = (E_11, E_22, E_33, 2 E_23, 2 E_13, 2 E_12) of a G-L strain E; stresses use the ASE sign (tension positive) in eV/angstrom^3.

Mathematics

Coordinates q = (gamma, u) (6 + 3n): gamma the G-L strain of the cell, u (n x 3) Cartesian displacements, flattened atom-major. Deformed structure: cell L U, positions (r_k + u_k) U, U = (I + 2E)^(1/2) the symmetric stretch. W(q) = the potential's energy of the deformed structure. At q = 0 (float64): g = dW/dq: g_v = V sigma : X(e_v) (X(e_v) the tensor of the unit Voigt vector v), g_{6+3k+a} = -F_{k,a}; H = d2W/dq2 = [[K, Lam^T], [Lam, Phi]]: K (eV) the G-L strain block (no stress term), Lam (eV/angstrom) the mixed block (with the residual-force term), Phi (eV/angstrom^2) the force constants. MACE: every block by automatic differentiation of W through the model at the neighbour list of q = 0 (the radial envelopes vanish with two derivatives at the cutoff, so the fixed list gives exact second derivatives), U as its power series sum_j binom(1/2, j) (2E)^j to order 12 (exact through second order at E = 0); H symmetrized. Any other ASE calculator (hessian_fd): H[:, j] = (g(q + h_j e_j) - g(q - h_j e_j)) / 2h_j, h_j = 1e-3 for gamma and 1e-3 angstrom for u, symmetrized, with the gradient at a deformed structure dW/dgamma_v = V J tr(U^-1 sigma' U^-1 X(e_v)), dW/du_k = -F'_k U (sigma', F': stress and forces there). Retained modes (Kelvin scaling): S = diag(g_K / V^(1/3), I_3n), g_K = (1, 1, 1, sqrt 2, sqrt 2, sqrt 2), S H S = sum_k w_k v_k v_k^T, H_ret = S^-1 (sum over w_k > TOL of w_k v_k v_k^T) S^-1 (float64), TOL = 1e-3 eV/angstrom^2; n_neg = #{w_k < -TOL}, n_zero = #{|w_k| <= TOL}. Pairs: every (i, j, n) with 1e-6 < |(f_j + n - f_i) L| <= RC = 5 angstrom, once per unordered pair (j > i, or j = i with n in the positive half space). Images are enumerated for g = f - floor(f) within |m_k| <= ceil(RC |b_k|) + 1 (b_k the rows of L^-T) and expressed for f as given, n = m - floor(f_j) + floor(f_i). Own bonds: geometry.bonds(L, f) (first shell, 1.15 times each atom's nearest-neighbour distance, r_max 4.5). D3 relaxations (FixSymmetry 1e-3 angstrom, FrechetCellFilter, FIRE, fmax 0.01 eV/angstrom, at most 800 steps, in float32; a relaxation that stops at the limit is continued for at most 2000 float64 steps if the space group at its end equals the input's): (0) MACE-OMAT-0, (1) MACE-OMAT-0 plus D3(BJ) (PBE parameters, two-body, cutoff 40 bohr). T1 = E(L, L_1), T0 = E(L, L_0), D = T1 - T0, E(L, L') = 1/2 (L^-1 L' L'^T L^-T - I) (geometry.green); masks m = (c_1, c_0, c_1 and c_0) with c the convergence of each relaxation; a tensor without convergence is 0. Descriptors: MACE-OMAT-0 invariants of every layer (float16); eSEN-30M-OMat: the l = 0 row of the node embedding after each of its 10 blocks (1280 per atom), averaged over the structure and its inversion image (fractional coordinates -f mod 1, same cell): x_i = [s_i(S) + s_i(I S)] / 2, invariant under O(3).

docs.title: recast.contract
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Contract checks of a featurizer (recast.featurizers): the symmetries and units its inputs must have for the networks, measured on one structure. tests/test_featurizer_contract.py applies them to the shipped featurizers and to the template; run them on a new potential before training with it.

Conventions: Z atomic numbers, f fractional coordinates (n x 3), L cell rows (angstrom). A transformation (Q, t), Q orthogonal (det +1 a rotation, det -1 an improper operation) and t a fractional translation, maps the structure to (Z, f + t, L Q^T), so that r -> r Q^T + t L Q^T.

Mathematics

Kelvin basis of symmetric strains B_1..3 = e_i e_i^T, B_4 = (e_2 e_3^T + e_3 e_2^T)/sqrt 2, B_5, B_6 likewise; Kelvin representation of Q K_ab = _F (orthogonal 6 x 6) Kelvin scaling of the G-L Hessian S = diag(1, 1, 1, sqrt 2, sqrt 2, sqrt 2, I_3n): H_K = S H S (H in q = (gamma, u), gamma the engineering Voigt vector of the G-L strain) expected transformation x' = x (descriptors); H_K' = R H_K R^T, R = diag(K, B), B = I_n kron Q (the deformed structures of q and of q' = (K gamma_K, u Q^T) are images of each other, so W'(q') = W(q)); relaxation strains T' = Q T Q^T violation of a quantity X v(X) = max |X' - X_expected| / max |X|, reported per block K, Lam, Phi units (h = 1e-3; W(q) the energy of the cell L U and positions (r + u) U, U = (I + 2E(gamma))^(1/2)): K[v, v] = (W(h e_v) - 2 W(0) + W(-h e_v)) / h^2 (gamma component v) Phi[a, a] = (W(h e_a) - 2 W(0) + W(-h e_a)) / h^2 (u coordinate a, h in angstrom) Lam[a, v] = (W(h e_v + h e_a) - W(h e_v - h e_a) - W(-h e_v + h e_a) + W(-h e_v - h e_a)) / (4 h^2) The second differences have an O(h^2) truncation (about 1e-6 relative).

docs.title: recast.geometry
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Geometry of crystal structures used by the correction: cells, fractional coordinates, the Green-Lagrange strain between two cells and its volume and shape readouts, engineering Voigt vectors and first-shell bonds.

Conventions

L cell matrix (3 x 3, angstrom); its rows are the lattice vectors a_1, a_2, a_3 f fractional coordinates (n x 3); Cartesian positions r = f L (angstrom) G metric tensor G = L L^T (angstrom^2); cell volume V = |det L| (angstrom^3)

Mathematics

Green-Lagrange (G-L) strain from a reference cell L_ref to a target cell L_tgt, in the Cartesian frame of L_ref: C = L_ref^-1 G_tgt L_ref^-T = I + 2E, E = 1/2 (C - I). C is the right Cauchy-Green tensor: if L_tgt = L_ref U R with U symmetric positive definite and R orthogonal, then C = U^2, so the stretch U = (I + 2E)^(1/2) rebuilds the target, L_tgt = L_ref U R. A strain E is admissible when lambda_min(I + 2E) > LAM_MIN = 1e-6; otherwise no cell has it. Volume and shape of E (the paper's error measures read these; they do not depend on the strain measure): J = det(I + 2E)^(1/2) = V_tgt / V_ref, S(E) = 1/2 ln(J^(-2/3) (I + 2E)) (symmetric, traceless). Engineering Voigt vector of a symmetric strain: gamma(E) = (E_11, E_22, E_33, 2 E_23, 2 E_13, 2 E_12). First-shell bonds of atom i: every pair (j, image n) with d_ijn = |(f_j + n - f_i) L| <= 1.15 min_{(j', n') != (i, 0)} d_ij'n', searched over the images n of a box sized for a radius r_max = 4.5 angstrom. The shell is that of atom i, so the list is not symmetric in i and j in general. Unwrapping: each fractional position is moved to the periodic image nearest a reference position, f <- f_ref + (f - f_ref) - round(f - f_ref).

docs.text:

docs.text:
First-shell bonds of a structure: array (n_bonds x 6) of (i, j, n_1, n_2, n_3, d) with d in angstrom.

The bond vector of a row is (f_j + n - f_i) L. The shell is defined per atom, against that atom's own nearest neighbour, so (i, j, n) is listed without (j, i, -n) when d_ijn exceeds 1.15 times the nearest-neighbour distance of j. The images searched are the box |n_k| <= ceil(r_max |b_k|) (1 / |b_k| is the spacing of the lattice planes k); the factor fac = 1.15 admits the distances up to 15 % above the nearest one.

docs.title: recast.targets
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Targets of a structure pair: the Green-Lagrange (G-L) strain E and the displacements u_k that carry a calculated structure (a DFT or MLIP relaxation) onto the experimental one, with the checks that decide in which description of the experimental structure the target is taken and whether the displacement target is usable.

Conventions (as geometry.py): L cell rows (angstrom), f fractional coordinates (n x 3), Z atomic numbers. The two structures list the same atoms in the same order (as in the paper's matched pairs; the checks below decide whether the displacement target is usable).

Mathematics

Unwrapping: the calculated coordinates are moved to the periodic images nearest the experimental ones, f_c <- f_e + (f_c - f_e) - round(f_c - f_e). Changes of basis: the set UNI of integer matrices M with entries in {-1, 0, 1} and |det M| = 1, in the order of itertools.product((-1, 0, 1), repeat=9) (the identity is one of them, index IDENT). The experimental cell in basis M is M L_e (rows), with fractional coordinates f_e M^-1. Strain norm of basis M (the distance between the two cells that decides the basis): with lam_i the eigenvalues of L_c^-1 (M G_e M^T) L_c^-T (G_e = L_e L_e^T), the norm of the log stretch, |eps_M|_F = sqrt(1/4 sum_i (ln lam_i)^2). Displacements of the stored correspondence: du_k = f_c,k - f_e,k, t = mean_k du_k (mean translation), disp_k = |(du_k - t) L_c|, rms_id = sqrt(mean_k disp_k^2) (angstrom). Swapped atoms: an atom whose nearest same-species experimental site (minimum image over the 27 neighbouring images, after removing t) is not its own. Flag (the description is checked further): |eps_M|_F < 0.99 |eps_I|_F for some M != I, or a swapped atom, or max_k disp_k > 0.5 angstrom. For a flagged pair (variants): best_match(f_m) = min over origins t (anchored on the rarest species) and same-species assignments (Hungarian algorithm on the minimum-image distances) of sqrt(mean_k |(f_c,k - f_m,pi(k) - t) L_c|^2), with one re-centring of t on the matched sites; rms_perm = best_match(f_e); candidates: the 24 bases with the smallest |eps_M|_F among those below 0.99 |eps_I|_F; for each, rms_M = best_match(f_e M^-1 mod 1); the basis k_alt with the smallest rms_M (first in order on ties). Strain target: E = green(L_c, L_e) = 1/2 (L_c^-1 G_e L_c^-T - I) (geometry.green), and r = rms_id; for a flagged pair r = min(r, rms_perm), and if a candidate exists and rms_alt < r - 0.02 or (rms_alt <= r + 0.02 and |eps_alt|_F < |eps_I|_F): E = green(L_c, UNI[k_alt] L_e), r = rms_alt, alt = True. The pair is rearranged when r > 0.3 angstrom. Displacement target, in the frame of the calculated cell (stored basis and atom order): u_k = (f_e,k - f_c,k) L_c - mean_k (f_e,k - f_c,k) L_c (angstrom), usable (pos_ok) when alt is False, sqrt(mean_k |u_k|^2) <= 0.3 angstrom and no atom other than H moves more than 1 angstrom. Target vector q = (gamma(E), u*) in R^(6 + 3n), gamma the engineering Voigt vector.

docs.title: strain_norms(L_ref, L_tgt)
docs.text:
Frobenius norms (len(UNI),) of the log stretches from L_ref to M L_tgt for every change of basis M in UNI.

lam_i are the eigenvalues of L_ref^-1 (M L_tgt L_tgt^T M^T) L_ref^-T; |eps|_F = sqrt(sum_i (ln lam_i / 2)^2).

docs.title: rms_identity(L, f_e, f_c)
docs.text:
Root-mean-square displacement (angstrom) of the stored correspondence, the mean translation removed.

du_k = f_c,k - f_e,k (fractional), Cartesian through the cell L (rows); the mean over the atoms is removed first.

docs.title: sites(L, Z, f_e, f_c)
docs.text:
Site checks of the stored correspondence: (max_k disp_k, |t L|, number of swapped atoms, max own / other).

t = mean_k (f_c,k - f_e,k) is the mean translation (fractional); disp_k = |(f_c,k - f_e,k - t) L| (angstrom). For each species with two or more atoms, the minimum-image distance (27 neighbouring images) of every calculated site, shifted by -t, to every experimental site of that species: an atom is swapped when another site is nearer than its own; worst is the largest ratio of the own distance to the nearest other one.

docs.title: mindist(L, f_a, f_b)
docs.text: Minimum-image distances (angstrom) between every site of f_a (n_a x 3) and every site of f_b (n_b x 3).

docs.title: best_match(L, Z, f_c, f_m)
docs.text:
Smallest root-mean-square displacement (angstrom) between two descriptions of a structure in the cell L.

Origins: t = f_c,a0 - f_m,j for the first atom a0 of the rarest species and every atom j of that species. For each origin, per species the assignment that minimizes the summed squared minimum-image distances is found with the Hungarian algorithm; t is then shifted by the mean residual of the matched sites and the assignment repeated once.

docs.title: variants(Z, L_e, f_e, L_c, f_c)
docs.text:
Other descriptions of the experimental structure for a flagged pair (a dict of floats and ints).

eps_id = |eps_I|_F, rms_id (rms_identity), rms_perm (best_match over origins and assignments in the stored basis), n_alt (number of candidate bases), and for the best candidate k_alt (index in UNI, -1 when there is none), eps_alt (its strain norm), rms_alt (its best_match) and det_alt (its determinant, +-1). Candidates are taken in order of increasing strain norm (a stable argsort), at most 24; a later candidate replaces the best only if strictly closer.

docs.title: flagged(Z, L_e, f_e, L_c, f_c)
docs.text: True when the stored description of the pair must be checked against its variants (module docstring).

docs.title: strain_target(L_e, f_e, L_c, f_c, var=None)
docs.text:
Strain target E* (3 x 3, G-L, frame of L_c), the matching rms r (angstrom) and whether another basis is used.

var: the variants() of a flagged pair, or None. Without it r = rms_identity and the stored basis is used; with it r = min(rms_identity, rms_perm), and the best candidate basis replaces the stored one when rms_alt < r - 0.02, or rms_alt <= r + 0.02 and its strain norm is below the stored one's (0.02 angstrom tolerance on the rms).

docs.title: displacement_target(Z, f_e, L_c, f_c, alt)
docs.text:
Displacement target u* (n x 3, angstrom, frame of L_c, mean removed), pos_ok, its rms and its largest non-H norm.

f_c must already be unwrapped against f_e. pos_ok requires the stored basis (alt False), sqrt(mean_k |u_k|^2) <= 0.3 angstrom and max_k |u_k| <= 1 angstrom over the atoms other than H (0 when there are none).

docs.title: targets(L_c, f_c, Z, L_e, f_e)
docs.text:
Targets of one structure pair (calculated L_c, f_c; experimental L_e, f_e; the same atoms in the same order).

Returns a dict with E (3 x 3), u (n x 3, angstrom), q (6 + 3n,), f_c (the unwrapped calculated coordinates), rms (the matching rms of the strain target, angstrom), alt, rearranged (rms > 0.3), pos_ok, flagged and variants (the variants() dict, or None when the pair is not flagged).

docs.title: recast.networks
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

The networks of the correction and the batches they read: the direct strain head (StrainNet; estimator 1 and the prior of estimator 5), the pair head (DLSNet; estimators 2 to 4 and the atoms), and the unified module of estimator 5 (UnifiedNet). Parameter names and shapes are those of the trained models, so their state dicts load unchanged.

A structure enters as a record (collate): n number of atoms; desc dict backbone name -> raw per-atom descriptors x_i (n x D, float32) of a pretrained MLIP; pairs (P, 2) local atom indices (i, j) of the pairs within r_c = 5 angstrom (each pair once, with its image); pv (P, 3) pair vectors v_p = (f_j + image - f_i) L (angstrom, float64; L rows are lattice vectors); pbeu Hubbard-U flag chi_U (1.0 for PBE+U, else 0.0); tx, txm (K, 3, 3) relaxation strains T_k (Green-Lagrange, Cartesian frame of the calculated cell) and their masks m_k (K,); H ((6 + 3n) x (6 + 3n)) Green-Lagrange Hessian on the retained modes, H_ret of recast.features (members with a Hessian only; eV in the engineering Voigt strain gamma, eV / angstrom^2 in the displacements u, eV / angstrom in the mixed block); kept in float64 in the batch; rides optional (R, 3) rows (H atom, neighbour, weight) of the riding model (unused by the final members).

Under a rotation R of the structure T_i -> R T_i R^T, T_k -> R T_k R^T, so E_d -> R E_d R^T. Pair head (DLSNet): Q_i^k = sum over the pairs containing i of f_k(p) dev(r_hat_p r_hat_p^T), f_k(p) = MLP_q(h_i + h_j, h_i * h_j, rbf(d_p)) f_c(d_p), k = 1..K (channel quadrupoles) quadrupole invariants of p: o_i^k + o_j^k, o_i^k o_j^k (o_i^k = r_hat_p^T Q_i^k r_hat_p), tr(Q_i^k Q_j^k), r_hat_p^T (Q_i^k Q_j^k + Q_j^k Q_i^k) r_hat_p / 2 tensor invariants of p: 100 m_k r_hat_p^T T_k r_hat_p, 100 m_k tr T_k, m_k (o_0, o_1) = MLP_p(h_i + h_j, h_i * h_j, rbf(d_p), quadrupole invariants, chi_U, g, tensor invariants) s_p = 1e-2 o_0 (target Green strain of the pair, (d'^2 / d^2 - 1) / 2), w_p = f_c(d_p) exp(clip(o_1, -3, 3)) spring scale kappa_0 = exp(theta) (eV) of the members with a Hessian (theta fixed or learned) Unified module (UnifiedNet, estimator 5): a strain head (context, graph trace), a pair head without its own spring scale, and a confidence head (z_V, z_S, z_K) = 4 tanh(MLP_c(xbar, chi_U) / 4) on the structure mean xbar of x~_i; with K = kappa exp(z_K) and S_w = K sum_p w_p, lam_V = S_w exp(z_V), lam_S = S_w exp(z_S) and (P H P + K A + Lam_d + Lam) q_hat = K r + Lam_d q_d, Lam_d = blockdiag(lam_V P_V + lam_S P_S, 0_3n), q_d = (gamma(E_d), 0), P_V = e e^T / 3, P_S = diag(1, 1, 1, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2) - P_V (e = (1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)), and A, r, Lam = diag(lam_g G_F, lam_u I) of recast.fits.normal_eq (gamma^T P_V gamma = (tr E)^2 / 3, gamma^T P_S gamma = |dev E|_F^2).

docs.title: recast.fits
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Least-squares fits that turn predicted pair-length changes into a deformation of the structure: the distance least-squares (DLS) fit and the Hessian-regularized DLS fit, batched over structures (torch, float64).

Coordinates of a structure with n atoms: q = (gamma, u) in R^(6 + 3n), with gamma the engineering Voigt vector of the Green-Lagrange (G-L) strain E of the cell and u the Cartesian displacements (angstrom) in the frame of the calculated structure. A batch pads every structure to M = 6 + 3 n_max coordinates; padded coordinates get identity rows and a zero right-hand side.

Mathematics

Pair p = (i, j, image) with vector v_p (angstrom), length d_p = |v_p|, direction r_hat_p = v_p / d_p. Green strain of its length under q, g_p = (d'_p^2 / d_p^2 - 1) / 2, to first order (exact at u = 0): a_p . q = r_hat_p^T E r_hat_p + r_hat_p . (u_j - u_i) / d_p, r_hat^T E r_hat = c_p . gamma, c_p = (x^2, y^2, z^2, yz, xz, xy) for r_hat = (x, y, z). Normal equations of the predicted changes s_p with weights w_p: A = sum_p w_p a_p a_p^T, r = sum_p w_p s_p a_p. Relative regularization (scale-free, so that a supercell gets the same fit): lam_g = LG sum_p w_p on gamma, in the Frobenius metric RG = diag(1, 1, 1, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2) lam_u = LU * 2 sum_p (w_p / d_p^2) / (3n) on u (the mean diagonal of A_uu, self-image pairs counted) DLS fit: (A + Lam) q_hat = r DLS fit of the cell (affine): (A_gg + lam_g RG) gamma_hat = r_g, u_hat = 0 Hessian-regularized DLS fit: q_hat = argmin_q 1/2 q^T H q + Delta E(q) + regularization (H: the retained-mode G-L Hessian H_ret of recast.features, float64), Delta E(q) = kappa_0 / 2 sum_p w_p (a_p . q - s_p)^2 (the missing energy; spring constants kappa_0 w_p), so that (P H P + kappa_0 A + Lam) q_hat = kappa_0 r, with Lam computed from the spring constants kappa_0 w_p and P = I - E E^T removing the three rigid translations E = (0_6; 1_n kron I_3) / sqrt(n) from the Hessian H. Limits: kappa_0 -> infinity gives the DLS fit; small kappa_0 gives the linear response kappa_0 H^+ r. Fit at a given cell gamma_c: u_hat = (A_uu + lam_u I)^-1 (r_u - A_ug gamma_c). Solves: M x = r by LU, accepted when |M x - r|_2 <= 1e-10 sqrt(m) (|M|_inf |x|_inf + |r|_inf) per system, else repeated on the CPU (and checked again). Gradients: dx = M^-1 (dr - dM x), so grad_r = M^-1 g, grad_M = -grad_r x^T.

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

The five strain estimators of the cell and their mean (Methods, Strain estimators), computed by trained members. A member is one trained network of one estimator, one initialization and one partition key, stored as its arguments (args_.json or args.json), weights (model_.pt) and training-set standardization (norm_.npz).

Mathematics (q = (gamma, u), gamma the engineering Voigt vector of the Green-Lagrange (G-L) strain E(gamma) of the cell, u the Cartesian displacements in angstrom; A, r, lam_g, lam_u, P H P from recast.fits.normal_eq with the pair targets s_p and weights w_p of the member's pair head and the G-L Hessian H, recast.networks): 1 direct strain head E_1 = E_d (networks.StrainNet) 2 DLS fit of the cell (A_gg + lam_g G_F) gamma = r_g, u = 0, G_F = diag(1, 1, 1, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2) 3 DLS fit (A + Lam) q = r, Lam = diag(lam_g G_F, lam_u I) 4 Hessian-regularized (P H P + kappa_0 A + Lam_kappa) q = kappa_0 r (weights kappa_0 w_p in A, r, Lam) DLS fit 5 with a strain prior (P H P + K A + Lam_d + Lam_K) q = K r + Lam_d q_d (networks.UnifiedNet) mean E_hat = (1 / M) sum_m E_m over the M members (five estimators times their initializations, and the partition keys for new structures; equal to the mean over the estimators of their means over initializations when every estimator has as many) E_r = E(gamma_r) of the solve for estimators 2 to 5. Estimators 1 and 5 contain the direct head; under a rotation R of the structure every estimate rotates as R E R^T.

docs.title: recast.losses
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Training losses of the correction: the cell loss of a predicted Green-Lagrange (G-L) strain, which is the loss of the paper's own volume and shape errors, and the atom loss of predicted displacements; both robust (pseudo-Huber) and averaged over the structures of a batch (torch).

Mathematics (E: G-L strain, 3 x 3, symmetric, in the frame of the calculated cell; C = I + 2E; gamma(E) its engineering Voigt vector): Pseudo-Huber function of a squared residual x^2 (quadratic below delta, linear above): rho_delta(x^2) = delta^2 (sqrt(1 + x^2 / delta^2) - 1). Volume and shape of E: ln J = 1/2 ln det C (ln of the volume ratio), S(E) = 1/2 ln(J^(-2/3) C) (traceless). Cell loss of a prediction E_hat with target E (w0 weights the volume part; every rotation-invariant quadratic form of a symmetric error combines a traceless and a scalar part, Schur's lemma, so one weight sets the balance): s2 = |S(E_hat) - S(E)|_F^2, t2 = w0 (ln J(E_hat) - ln J(E))^2 / 3, joint rho_delta(s2 + t2), decoupled rho_delta(s2) + rho_delta(t2). Evaluation in float64 without an eigendecomposition (finite gradients at degenerate eigenvalues; 3 x 3 determinants and inverses by cofactors): Cbar = J^(-2/3) C, Y = (Cbar - I)(Cbar + I)^-1 = tanh(S) (Cayley transform, symmetric), S = atanh(Y) = sum_{k=0}^{K-1} Y^(2k+1) / (2k+1) + R_K, |R_K|_F <= r^(2K+1) / ((2K+1)(1 - r^2)) if |Y|_F <= r; with |Y|_F <= R0 = 1/2 and K = 24 terms, |R_K|_F <= 4.8e-17. For |Y|_F > R0 (shapes far beyond the data): S = 2^j atanh(Y_j), Y_j the Cayley transform of Cbar^(1/2^j) (j square roots by the coupled Denman-Beavers iteration, each renormalized to det 1), j the smallest count with |Y_j|_F <= R0. Outside the domain (lambda_min(C) <= LAM_MIN = 1e-6, Sylvester's criterion) no structure has E_hat and the error measures are undefined; such a prediction gets the quadratic form of the same loss at its target, s2 = dgamma^T P_S(E) dgamma, t2 = w0 (v(E) . dgamma)^2 / 3, dgamma = gamma(E_hat) - gamma(E), the first-order expansion of the error measures about E (label_metric): finite, convex, pointing back inside. Label metric at E (C = I + 2E): d ln J = tr(C^-1 dE) = v . dgamma, v = gamma-dual of C^-1 (off-diagonal entries not doubled); d S = dev DLog_C[dE], gamma(dS) = Lt dgamma, P_S = Lt^T G_F Lt, G_F = diag(1, 1, 1, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2); DLog_C[Y] = Q (F o (Q^T Y Q)) Q^T for C = Q diag(c) Q^T, F_ab = (ln c_a - ln c_b) / (c_a - c_b), F_aa = 1 / c_a (Daleckii-Krein). Linearized relative change of the length of bond b = (i, j) with vector v_b = d_b r_hat_b (angstrom) under the coordinates q = (gamma, u) of the calculated structure (gamma: G-L strain in engineering Voigt form; u: Cartesian displacements): e_b(q) = [d_b r_hat_b^T E(gamma) r_hat_b + (u_j - u_i) . r_hat_b] / d_b. Atom loss of predicted coordinates q against the targets q (bond weights bw_b: 1 for bonds between atoms other than H, 0 for bonds to H; displacement weights um_k = 1 / (n' d_bar^2) on the coordinates of the n' atoms other than H, d_bar the mean first-shell bond length, 0 elsewhere): e_b = e_b(q) - e_b(q), L_b = sum_b bw_b e_b^2 / max(1, sum_b bw_b), joint rho_delta(L_g + wb L_b + wu sum um (q - q)^2), L_g = sum_k VW_k (gamma - gamma)_k^2, VW = (1, 1, 1, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2) (the Frobenius norm of the strain error in engineering Voigt form); decoupled rho_delta(wb L_b) + rho_delta(wu L_u), L_u = sum_k um_k |du_k - |^2, du = u_hat - u, = sum_k um_k du_k / sum_k um_k (the atoms are defined up to a translation, so the weighted mean is removed). With the atoms solved at the experimental cell (gamma = gamma), L_g = 0 and the joint atom loss is rho_delta(wb L_b + wu sum um (u_hat - u)^2), equation (lossat) of the paper's Methods. Every loss is the mean over the structures of the batch. COUNT keeps the number of predictions evaluated by the series, by the square roots and outside the domain since import.

docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Training of the members of the correction, one partition key at a time, as the paper's members were trained: the direct strain head (estimator 1), the pair heads of the DLS fits and of the Hessian-regularized DLS fit (estimators 2 to 4, and the atom fit), and the module of estimator 5. --preset selects the hyperparameters of one of the six member types of the final model (A0, aff, full, spr30, uni, sat); any of them can be overridden on the command line.

Training folder (the layout of recast.features plus the targets): train.h5 one group per structure key with Z (n,), f_dft (n, 3), L_dft (3, 3): the calculated structure (cell rows in angstrom); q (6 + 3n, float32): the target q = (gamma(E), u) of recast.targets (engineering Voigt vector of the Green-Lagrange (G-L) strain E, displacements in angstrom in the frame of the calculated cell); E (3, 3), optional: the strain target of estimator 1 (default E(gamma)); bonds (m, 5): the first-shell bonds (i, j, n1, n2, n3) of the experimental structure; H and desc (recast.features: the retained-mode G-L Hessian H_ret, float64, and the MACE-OMAT-0 descriptors); attributes V (angstrom^3), n_neg, n_zero and pos_ok (u usable) pairs.npz keys, pair_offset, pairs (i, j, n1, n2, n3) within rc, rc, functional (json: key -> PBE or PBE+U) tensors.npz mp_ids, T (N, K, 3, 3), mask (N, K), names: the G-L D3 relaxation strains (recast.features) desc_new.h5 eSEN descriptors (recast.features.write_esen_descriptors), only for members with backbone esen Partition file: json {key: {"train": [...], "val": [...], "test": [...]}} of structure keys; the three sets of a key must be disjoint and free of repeats (checked).

Mathematics (rho_delta(x^2) = delta^2 (sqrt(1 + x^2 / delta^2) - 1); q = (gamma, u); E(gamma) the G-L strain, U = (I + 2E)^(1/2)): labels E = E(gamma) and its label metric (v, P_S) (recast.losses.label_metric); per pair p = (i, j, n) with vector v_p, d_p = |v_p|: the Green strain s_p = (|(v_p + uj - u_i) U|^2 / d_p^2 - 1) / 2 for pairs without H of structures with pos_ok, weights sw_p = 1 / (number of such pairs of the structure), 0 otherwise; per first-shell bond b: bw_b = 1 for bonds without H of pos_ok structures, else 0; displacement weights um = 1 / (n' dbar^2) on the coordinates of the n' atoms other than H of pos_ok structures (dbar the mean bond length, angstrom), 0 elsewhere (recast.losses) cell loss recast.losses.cell_loss: the error-measure loss rho_delta(|S(E_hat) - S(E)|_F^2 + w0 (ln J_hat - ln J)^2 / 3) (joint) or its decoupled form, evaluated in float64 estimator 1 (StrainNet) loss = cell loss of E_d against E estimators 2 to 4 and the atom fit (DLSNet and recast.fits) q_hat = the free fit (cell only for estimator 2; with the Hessian H (float64) and the spring scale kappa_0 for estimator 4 and the atom fit); q_c = the fit at the experimental cell gamma (atoms "clamped") or q_hat (atoms "e2e"); loss = cell loss of q_hat + lam_at atom_loss(q_c) + lam_pair L_pair, L_pair = rho_pair(sum_p sw_p (s_p - s*_p)^2) over the structures with labelled pairs (unused, 0, in the final members); no atom term for estimator 2 estimator 5 (UnifiedNet) loss = cell loss of q_hat + lam_at atom_loss(q_hat or q_c) + lam_aux [cell loss of E_d + cell loss of q_p], q_p the Hessian-regularized DLS fit of the same pair head without the prior joint and decoupled forms of the cell and atom losses: recast.losses standardization x~ = (x - mu) / sd, mu and sd (+ 1e-6) over the atoms of the training structures (float32) optimizer AdamW (lr, weight decay wd), gradient norm clipped at 10, ReduceLROnPlateau (factor 0.5, patience 10) on the validation loss; a step with a non-finite loss or gradient is skipped (more than 2 % skipped stops the run); early stopping after patience epochs without a lower validation criterion (the total loss, or its cell part with select = cell) or after hours; the state of the best epoch is kept seeds torch.manual_seed(torch_seed) at the start of every key (initialization and any torch draw), numpy default_rng(key) for the batches batches estimator 1: a permutation of the training structures per epoch (rng = default_rng(key)) in chunks of bs, validation in chunks of 128 in set order; the others: chunks of bs structures sorted by atom count, in an order shuffled per epoch (same rng), validation in sorted chunks of 64 Outputs in --out: args.json, model_.pt (loadable by recast.estimators.Member), norm_.npz (mu, sd), val_.json (best criterion, its errors, epochs, skipped steps, per-epoch history, and the counts of the cell-loss evaluations by series, square roots and outside the domain), pred_.npz and predval_.npz (predictions E, u of the test and validation structures), test_.json (recast.score.variant_rows of PBE, cellO, model and cellO+model). Outputs that name structures are derived from the targets: keep them private. usage: python -m recast.train --preset spr30 --data DIR --partitions parts.json --keys 42 --out DIR [--torch-seed 0]

docs.title: recast.predict
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Predictions of the final correction for new calculated structures, and their outputs: the corrected structure (POSCAR and CIF), the atoms at a given cell, the per-pair length changes and the spread of the five strain estimates. The inputs are a features folder (recast.features: write_features and write_esen_descriptors) and a release folder of trained members (tools/export_release.py: manifest.json and members//{args,model,norm}_.*). No experimental quantity is read.

Mathematics (L: cell rows in angstrom; f: fractional coordinates, n x 3; Z: atomic numbers; strains are Green-Lagrange (G-L) strains E, 3 x 3, in the Cartesian frame of the input cell, with C = I + 2E, U = C^(1/2) the stretch and gamma = voigt(E) = (E_11, E_22, E_33, 2 E_23, 2 E_13, 2 E_12); u: displacements in angstrom): estimate r E_r = (1 / (S K)) sum_{s,k} E_{r,s,k}: the mean of estimator r (1 to 5, Methods) over its S initializations (member tags) and the K partition keys (recast.estimators.Member.cell) cell E_hat = (1/5) sum_r E_r (the mean over all cell members, as every estimator has S K of them) domain lambda_min(I + 2E_hat) <= LAM_MIN = 1e-6 means no cell has E_hat: the structure is then returned unchanged (E = 0, u = 0) and flagged invalid; lam_min is reported for every structure atoms u_hat = (1 / (S' K)) sum_{s,k} u_{s,k}(gamma_hat): the atom-fit members' Hessian-regularized DLS fit of the atoms at the cell gamma_hat (recast.atoms.atoms_at) structure L_hat = L U_hat, f_hat = f + u_hat L^-1, so that r_hat_k = (f_k L + u_hat_k) U_hat, U_hat = (I + 2E_hat)^(1/2); written with the atoms in the input order and f_hat wrapped to [0, 1) given cell a cell L_c (rows, in the lattice basis of L): E_c = 1/2 (L^-1 L_c L_c^T L^-T - I); or a G-L strain E_c (3 x 3, or its engineering Voigt vector) with L_c = L (I + 2E_c)^(1/2). The atoms u_c = u(gamma_c) of the atom-fit members are written with L_c and f + u_c L^-1. A cell whose log stretch 1/2 ln(I + 2E_c) has a principal value beyond 0.2 in magnitude is refused: it is then taken to be in another lattice basis spread s_S = ((1/5) sum_r |dev(E_r - E_hat)|F^2)^(1/2), s_V = std_r tr E_r (both in %) pairs for every pair p = (i, j, n) within 5 angstrom of the input, d_p = |(f_j + n - f_i) L| (angstrom): the realized Green strain 100 g_p, g_p = (d_hat_p^2 / d_p^2 - 1) / 2 (%), in the written structure; whether p is a first-shell bond of the input (recast.geometry.bonds, either orientation); the target 100 s_p (%, a Green strain) and the relative weight w_p / sum_p w_p of the pair heads of estimators 2, 3 and 4 (each averaged over its members), and the mean target. The targets are what the fits balance against each other and against the stiffness, not predictions of single distances summary volume change 100 (J_hat - 1), J = det(I + 2E)^(1/2) (%), shape change 100 |S(E_hat)|_F, S(E) = 1/2 ln(J^(-2/3) (I + 2E)) (%), the spreads, max_k |u_hat_k| (angstrom), lam_min, invalid, gamma_hat symmetrize (optional) E <- (1/|G|) sum_g R_g E R_g^T and u <- (1/|G|) sum_g T_g u, (T_g u){sigma_g(k)} = R_g u_k, over the space group G of the input at a tolerance t (group()); this removes the small asymmetry left by float32 networks and by inputs that are symmetric only to about t usage:

python -m recast.predict --release DIR --features DIR --out DIR [--given given.json] [--pairs]
                         [--symmetrize 1e-3] [--verify-release]

docs.title: recast.errors
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Error measures of a predicted structure against the experimental one, as reported in the paper. Every error compares two deformations of the same calculated structure: the target (E, u_k) and the prediction (E_hat, u_hat_k).

Conventions

L calculated cell (3 x 3, rows = lattice vectors, angstrom); r_k = f_k L its Cartesian positions E Green-Lagrange strain of the cell (3 x 3, symmetric, in the Cartesian frame of L); C = I + 2E, U = C^(1/2) the stretch, J = det(C)^(1/2), S(E) = 1/2 ln(J^(-2/3) C) (geometry.volume_shape) u_k Cartesian displacement of atom k (angstrom), in the frame of L The deformed structure has the cell L U and the positions (r_k + u_k) U (U is symmetric, so U^T = U).

Mathematics (per structure; the paper reports 100 x these as percentages): volume e_V = |J_hat / J - 1| = |V_hat / V - 1| shape e_S = |S(E_hat) - S(E)|_F lengths e_L = (1/3) sum_i |(G_hat_ii / G_ii)^(1/2) - 1|, G = L (I + 2E) L^T (lattice-vector lengths) angles e_A = (1/3) sum |arccos(c_hat) - arccos(c)| over the three cell angles (degrees), c = G_jk / sqrt(G_jj G_kk) bonds e_B = < |ln(d_hat_b / d_b)| > over the first-shell bonds b of the experimental structure without H, d_b = |(r_j + u_j) U + n L U - (r_i + u_i) U| for the bond (i, j, image n) bond angles e_theta = < |theta_hat - theta| > (degrees) over the pairs of distinct bonds without H at a shared atom positions e_D = ((1/n') sum_{k not H} |du_k - |^2)^(1/2), du = u_hat - u, the mean over the n' atoms other than H (the rigid translation removed)

L (n, 3, 3) are the calculated cells, E_true and E_hat (n, 3, 3) the target and predicted G-L strains in their frames (both admissible). The metric of a deformed cell is G = L (I + 2E) L^T; the cosines of the angles are clipped to [-1, 1] before arccos.

docs.title: recast.score
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

Scores of predicted structures against the experimental ones on test sets, and the statistics of the paper: per structure the cell and atom errors of the prediction and of the references; per partition the mean over its scored test structures, then the mean and standard deviation over the partitions; the corrected resampled t-test of paired fold differences; the cluster bootstrap of a mean difference and of a relative change.

Conventions: L calculated cell (rows, angstrom), f fractional coordinates (n x 3), Z atomic numbers; a deformation of the calculated structure is q = (gamma, u), gamma the engineering Voigt vector of the Green-Lagrange (G-L) strain E(gamma) and u (n x 3, angstrom) the displacements in the frame of L; the target is q = (gamma, u), E = E(gamma*); U = (I + 2E)^(1/2), J = det(I + 2E)^(1/2). bonds are the first-shell bonds (i, j, n1, n2, n3) of the experimental structure. Domain rule: a predicted E with lambda_min(I + 2E) <= 1e-6 has no structure and is scored as the calculated structure (E = 0, u = 0).

Mathematics

variant errors of a deformation q (percent): vol 100 |J / J - 1| axis 100 (1/3) sum_i |ln(|a_i U| / |a_i U|)|, a_i the rows of L bond, bondXH, angle, disp recast.errors.atom_errors (only when the displacement target is usable) cell errors of a predicted strain (recast.errors.cell_errors): cell:vol, cell:shape, cell:len in percent and cell:ang in degrees; the same for E = 0: PBE:vol_cell, PBE:shape, PBE:len, PBE:ang variants of a test structure: PBE (q = 0), cellO (gamma, u = 0), full (gamma_hat, u_hat(gamma_hat)), cellO+final (gamma, u_hat(gamma*)), gamma_hat = gamma(E_hat) summary over partitions k = 1..K with scored test sets T_k (excluded structures left out): m_k(x) = mean over T_k of x (missing values skipped); mean = (1/K) sum_k m_k; sd = sample standard deviation of the m_k (ddof 1); the median over all scored rows; bands of the uncorrected shape error PBE:shape (< 1, 1 to 3, >= 3 %) with the means of cell:shape, PBE:shape and cell:vol; bonds to H over the neutron rows corrected resampled t-test (Nadeau and Bengio 2003) of fold mean differences d_j, j = 1..J, test and training sizes n2, n1: t = dbar / sqrt((1/J + n2/n1) s_d^2) with J - 1 degrees of freedom; two-sided p = 2 P(T > |t|), one-sided p = P(T > t) for an increase cluster bootstrap over groups g (S_c(g), S_r(g) the sums of corrected and reference errors of the structures in g, n(g) their number): B draws of G groups with replacement (counts w_b(g)), d_b = sum_g w_b (S_c - S_r) / sum_g w_b n, r_b = 100 (sum_g w_b S_c / sum_g w_b S_r - 1), 95 % intervals from the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles over b; B = 10,000, numpy default_rng(20261028)

docs.title: recast.pipeline
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

The training pipeline from structure pairs to a release, as functions behind the recast commands: targets pairs (calculated and experimental structure, same atoms in the same order) -> targets.h5 (recast.targets) features targets.h5 -> a training folder: the inputs of the calculated structures (recast.featurizers) with the targets; optionally one shard of the structures (index i mod n = I), resumable, and the merge of the shards into one folder (the same folder as one run) split partitions {key: {train, val, test}} (recast.partitions) members the 18 members of every key: six member types (recast.train presets) times three initializations jobs the same training as one command line per member type, initialization and key (for a job array) select the candidate run with the lowest development error (one metric for all candidates) export trained members -> a release folder (manifest.json, members/), the input of recast.predict score the release's test errors on each key's own test set (recast.score)

Conventions as recast.targets and recast.train (L cell rows in angstrom, f fractional coordinates, q = (gamma, u) with gamma the engineering Voigt vector of the Green-Lagrange strain E and u the displacements in angstrom).

Mathematics

shards shard I of n holds the training structures (sorted keys of targets.h5, rearranged pairs left out) of index i with i mod n = I; the merge restores that sorted order partitions recast.partitions (test splits, development folds, grouped folds, fractions) selection J(c) = (1/K) sum_k mean over the test structures of key k of the metric of candidate c (for example cell:shape = 100 e_S of the cell, or cellO+final:bond = 100 e_B of the atoms at the experimental cell); the chosen candidate minimizes J, ties to the first listed ensemble per key k: E_hat = (1/15) sum over the cell members of key k of E_m, u_hat the mean of the three atom-fit members' atoms at gamma(E_hat), u_c their atoms at the experimental cell gamma* (recast.predict with keys = [k]); errors recast.score.structure_row, summary recast.score.summarize

docs.title: recast.toy
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

A small synthetic set of structure pairs for the tutorial and the pipeline test: ASE prototypes of seven metals and their alloys as the calculated structures, each deformed by a known strain and known displacements as its experimental structure, and toy featurizers (ASE's EMT potential, radial descriptors). No external data; the numbers mean nothing physical.

Conventions: L cell rows (angstrom), f fractional coordinates (n x 3); r = f L.

Mathematics

calculated L_c, f_c of an ASE prototype (fcc, bcc, hcp, B2, L1_2, L1_0) at lattice constants that give every atom the volume v(Z) of its fcc reference state (ASE's reference data) strain E = (e_V / 3) I + e_S (3 z z^T - I) / 2 (a Green-Lagrange strain), z = the unit vector along the third cell row, e_V = -(1/n) sum_k c(Z_k) (the volume change, c(Z) = 0.010 to 0.045 per element), e_S = 0.004 for the hexagonal and tetragonal cells, else 0 displacements u_k drawn from N(0, (0.01 angstrom)^2) per component (seeded by the structure index), the mean removed: u_k <- u_k - (1/n) sum_l u_l; none for one-atom cells experimental L_e = L_c U, f_e = f_c + u L_c^-1, so that r_e,k = (r_c,k + u_k) U, U = (I + 2E*)^(1/2)

docs.title: recast.cli
docs.text:
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT Utkarsh Singh: github.com/utksi

The recast command. recast correct corrects one calculated structure with the released networks; the other subcommands run the training pipeline (recast.pipeline) and pass their options on to recast.train, recast.predict and recast.score. No mathematics of its own: each subcommand calls the function named in its help.

usage:

recast correct STRUCTURE [--source dft|tece_oam_rra|equflashv2_oam] [--functional PBE|PBE+U] [--given FILE]
               [--symmetrize TOL] -o OUT
recast toy -o pairs.json
recast targets PAIRS.json -o targets.h5
recast features targets.h5 -o DATA [--inputs shipped|toy|MODULE:FUNCTION] [--device cuda] [--shard I/N] [--resume]
recast features targets.h5 -o DATA --merge SHARD [SHARD ...]
recast groups DATA -o groups.csv
recast split DATA -o parts.json [--keys 42,...,51] [--test 0.1] [--val 0.1] [--order FILE] [--units FILE]
recast folds --partitions parts.json --groups groups.csv -o folds.json [--random 3000,3010] [--formula 3100]
             [--prototype 3200] [--seed 20261022] [--units FILE] [--add-to FOLDS]
recast grouped DATA --groups groups.csv -o grouped.json [--prototype 4200] [--chemsys 4300] [--units FILE]
recast fraction parts.json -o frac.json --fraction 0.25 [--seed 0] [--keys K,...]
recast table --splits parts.json --folds folds.json [grouped.json ...] [--columns ids.csv] -o pairs.csv
recast members --data DATA --partitions parts.json --keys 42 --runs RUNS [--presets ...] [-- recast.train options]
recast jobs --data DATA --partitions parts.json --keys 42,43 --runs RUNS -o lines.txt [--sbatch FILE --account A
            --partition P --time T] [-- recast.train options]
recast train | predict | score ...   (the module's own options)
recast select --data DATA --keys 42 --metric cell:shape RUN [RUN ...]
recast export --runs RUNS --keys 42 --data DATA -o RELEASE
recast evaluate --release RELEASE --data DATA --partitions parts.json --keys 42 -o scores.json

Correct one structure with the released networks (recast.correction.correct).

Option Meaning STRUCTURE calculated structure: POSCAR, CIF or any file ASE reads --source dft (default), tece_oam_rra or equflashv2_oam: what relaxed the structure --functional PBE (default) or PBE+U, for a DFT structure --given FILE place the atoms also at this cell: JSON {"cell": ...} or a Green-Lagrange {"strain": ...}, or a structure file --symmetrize TOL project the correction onto the input's space group at TOL angstrom -o, --out output folder --release DIR local release folder (default: download utksi/recast-models) --mace FILE mace-omat-0-medium.model (default: download) --workdir DIR keep the computed features in this folder --inputs SPEC featurizers: shipped (default, every input from MACE-OMAT-0), toy, or MODULE:FUNCTION for a release trained with your own --threads N PyTorch threads (0: PyTorch's default)

Subcommand Options Function recast toy -o, --out recast.toy.write_toy_pairs recast targets PAIRS, -o, --out recast.pipeline.make_targets recast features TARGETS, -o, --out, --inputs, --mace, --device, --shard I/N, --resume; or --merge SHARD ... recast.pipeline.write_training_folder, recast.pipeline.merge_training_folders recast members --data, --partitions, --keys, --runs, --seeds, --presets, --device, then -- and recast train options recast.pipeline.train_members recast jobs --data, --partitions, --keys, --runs, --seeds, --presets, --device, --command, -o, --out, --sbatch, --account, --partition, --time, --cpus, --gpus, --mem, --setup, --name, then -- and recast train options recast.pipeline.job_lines, recast.pipeline.slurm_script recast select RUN ..., --data, --keys, --metric recast.pipeline.select recast export --runs, --keys, --data, --name, -o, --out recast.pipeline.export_release recast evaluate --release, --data, --partitions, --keys, -o, --out recast.pipeline.score_release

recast features --shard I/N computes the structures of index i with i mod N = I (in the sorted order of the structure keys) into its own folder, which is a training folder of those structures; --resume continues an interrupted run in the same folder; --merge joins the finished shard folders into the folder of one run. recast jobs writes one recast train line per member type, seed and key (and, with --sbatch, a Slurm array script that runs line SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID + 1); it never submits anything. Lines of one run folder may run at the same time: each writes only the files of its key.

Subcommand Options Function recast groups DATA, -o, --out recast.partitions.group_table recast split DATA, -o, --out, --keys, --test, --val, --order, --units recast.partitions.test_splits recast folds --partitions, --keys, --groups, -o, --out, --random, --formula, --prototype, --seed, --units, --add-to recast.partitions.development_folds, recast.partitions.add_families recast grouped DATA, --groups, -o, --out, --prototype, --chemsys, --units recast.partitions.grouped_folds recast fraction PARTITIONS, -o, --out, --fraction, --seed, --keys recast.partitions.fraction recast table --splits, --split-keys, --folds, --fold-keys, --id-name, --columns, -o, --out recast.partitions.write_table

--units FILE (a CSV with columns key,unit) keeps the pairs of one unit on one side of every partition, for example several experimental reports of one material. --order FILE lists the pairs in the order that defines the permutation of recast split (default: the sorted keys). recast folds draws the development folds inside the pairs that are in no test set of --partitions; the families are drawn in the order random, formula, prototype with one generator.
